anita: Quick question for SDK owners — who should own the canonical mapping of API error shapes -> client exceptions? Also looking for guidance on request-id propagation and what to log at debug level.

sam: I think SDK team owns the surface, but runtime/infra should own the canonical header name and propagation. agree we need a single source. :+1:

leo: From a concrete point: map 4xx -> ClientError subclasses, 5xx -> ServerError, 429 -> RateLimitError (include retry-after). For streaming: if connection drops mid-stream, raise StreamAborted with original request_id attached.

marta: +1. Can we standardize on `x-request-id` rather than ad-hoc names? puts everyone on the same page for logs. Also recommend `x-rw-request-id` if we want uniqueness for Redwood traces vs customer headers.

anita: Good call. If we pick `x-rw-request-id` can infra populate that if missing?

sdk-oncall-bot: infra will backfill `x-rw-request-id` at the edge when absent. Logs will include it as `rw.request_id` field.

ben: Language specifics: Python SDK should expose a base exception `RedwoodError(Exception)` with typed subclasses: `BadRequestError`, `AuthError`, `RateLimitError(retry_after)`, `ServerError`. Set `err.request_id` attribute and `err.status_code`. Node SDK: set `err.code` string and `err.requestId` for parity.

leo: Example mapping snippet for docs (keep short):
```
HTTP 400 -> BadRequestError
HTTP 401 -> AuthError
HTTP 403 -> PermissionError
HTTP 404 -> NotFoundError
HTTP 429 -> RateLimitError (include Retry-After)
HTTP 5xx -> ServerError
stream disconnect -> StreamAborted (attach partial response + request_id)
```

marta: Logging guidance: always log `request_id` at INFO+ (so support engineers can grep), log full headers+body only at DEBUG. For structured logs: logger.info("call complete", {"request_id": rid, "model": model, "latency_ms": lat}).

anita: How about retries? who owns default policies? client or server?

sam: Default: SDKs implement idempotent-safe retries for transient network errors and 5xx. Do NOT automatically retry 4xx except 429. Respect `Retry-After`. Make retry backoff jittered. Allow users to opt-out / provide custom policy.

ben: For streaming we need special behavior: don't auto-retry resumed streams; instead surface a resumable cursor if supported. Otherwise raise StreamAborted with `can_retry: false` so caller can decide.

leo: Debug flag: add env var `RW_SDK_DEBUG=1` to dump request/response headers and `x-rw-request-id`. Keep dumps short, one line per header. Also include curl command to reproduce.

marta: Small PR todo: add `request_id` to all exception constructors + include in `__str__`/`message` so it's visible in logs.

anita: I'm going to open a tiny ADR-ish doc and a PR. Who wants review for the Python shape?

ben: Happy to review Python.

leo: I'll look at the Node/TS shape.

sdk-oncall-bot: Assigned: @ben review -> PR 3421, @leo review -> PR 3422. Reminder: attach a unit test that asserts `err.request_id` is present and that `RateLimitError.retry_after` parses both seconds and HTTP-date.

anita: Thanks all. I'll draft the doc and ping when PRs exist. If anyone has existing patterns in repos, drop links here.

sam: dropping link to internal gist with a minimal exception hierarchy: https://internal.gists/redwood/err-shape-2026

marta: Also adding a short checklist for oncall: 1) grep logs for `rw.request_id`, 2) if 5xx spike -> check infra routing, 3) if many 429s -> evaluate client-side rate limiting.

anita: perfect. end of thread.
